subscribe.title: Subscribe to the calendar
subscribe.intro: Put game release dates in your own calendar. Subscribe once and delays, cancellations and date changes show up in the same calendar automatically, with nothing to re-import.

delay.title: Updates take time
delay.body: Our data updates right away, but calendar apps only check for new content now and then. Google Calendar usually takes hours between refreshes (about 5 to 6 hours in our tests) and cannot be refreshed manually; Apple Calendar can refresh at once if you pull down on the calendar list; Outlook usually takes hours too. Treat this as a release-date reminder, not a live notification.

changes.title: How changes look in your calendar
changes.intro: Once subscribed, changes to a game show up on the same calendar event, with no duplicates.
changes.postponed: Delayed with no new date: the event stays on its old date and its title gets a “[Delayed: date TBA]” prefix.
changes.cancelled: Cancelled: Google Calendar removes the event; Apple Calendar keeps it and shows it struck through.
changes.rescheduled: Date changed: the same event moves to the new date, with no duplicate.

clients.title: How to subscribe in each calendar

apple.title: Apple Calendar (iPhone, iPad, Mac)
apple.s1: Use “Open in calendar app” above. Or in Calendar on Mac choose File → New Calendar Subscription. On iPhone or iPad (iOS/iPadOS 26) go to Settings → Apps → Calendar → Calendar Accounts → Add Account → Other → Add Subscribed Calendar (on older versions: Settings → Calendar → Accounts → Add Account → Other → Add Subscribed Calendar).
apple.s2: Paste the subscription URL and choose Subscribe.
apple.s3: You can change the refresh rate in the subscription's settings; to refresh right away, pull down on the calendar list.

google.title: Google Calendar
google.s1: Open Google Calendar on the web from a computer.
google.s2: Next to “Other calendars” on the left, click “+” and choose “From URL”.
google.s3: Paste the subscription URL and click “Add calendar”.
google.note: The mobile app cannot add a calendar from a URL; once you add it on the web, the app on your phone shows it too, on the same Google account. Google usually refreshes subscriptions only every few hours (about 5 to 6 hours in our tests), and there is no manual refresh.

outlook.title: Outlook
outlook.s1: On the web: open Calendar and choose Add calendar → Subscribe from web.
outlook.s2: Paste the subscription URL, give it a name and import.
outlook.s3: Outlook decides the refresh interval, usually a few hours.

realtime.title: Want instant alerts?
realtime.body: Calendar subscriptions are not instant. We plan to offer email and Discord direct-message alerts later, so you hear about a delay right away.
